How to handle rejection
without losing confidence
Remember it's one opinion, not the truth. A job, a date, a team. One person's no says more about their needs than about your worth.
Feel it, then set a limit. Be disappointed for an evening. Then decide the next step the following morning. Don't let it drag for weeks.
Ask what you can learn. Was it timing, preparation, fit? A calm look at what happened turns a rejection into useful information.
Keep the number of attempts high. The men who succeed hear no more often than anyone else. They simply keep going. Hearing no is part of the game.
Try this for 30 days: five minutes a day of history, art or science. Growing every day reminds you your value doesn't depend on one answer.
slides.texte_sophia: Try this for 30 days: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Growing every day reminds you your value doesn't depend on one answer.

slides.texte_overlay: Talk to someone who believes in you. A friend, a brother, a mentor. Hearing your strengths out loud rebuilds confidence fast. Confidence comes back quickly.
Be gracious. "Thanks for the chance, good luck." Handling a no with class leaves doors open and shows real confidence. Then move on to the next chance with your head up.
